title: Per-route & model slice rollup summarizer with federated rollups
creator: Priya Natarajan
description: Design and implement a resilient summarization service that computes per-route / per-model / per-customer micro-rollups for cost and latency. The service should produce compact, queryable artifacts (hourly and 5m rollups) usable by Console dashboards, billing exports, and SLO evaluators. The focus is on federated, tenant-aware aggregation to minimize tail-cardinality and support streaming-friendly increments and efficient backfills.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Service emits hourly and 5-minute rollup artifacts for route+model+tenant with fields: token_count, compute_ms, avg_latency_ms, p95_latency_ms, request_count, sample_weight.
2) Aggregates are namespace-sharded for tenants and writable to object store and a fast read index (BigTable-like).
3) Console dashboards can query 30-day rollups within 5s for typical queries.
4) Backfill process can populate historical windows with less than 2x compute overhead.
5) No data loss for >=99.9% of incoming trace-linked telemetry in steady-state.
6) Integration tests and a staged rollout (canary) documented and executed.
implementation_notes:
Overview: Implement a two-path pipeline: 1) streaming micro-aggregator that consumes trace-linked telemetry (span events + runtime tags) and emits delta updates to a change-log topic; 2) rollup worker that materializes time-windowed summaries with tenant sharding and idempotent writes.

Key design decisions: use sample-weighted counters to reconcile sampled traces; store both incremental deltas and compact checkpoints every hour; make rollups append-only with tombstones for corrections. Prefer vectorized map-reduce over per-request writes to the index.

Storage: rollup artifacts written to GCS in Parquet for long-term retention and to a low-latency key-value store for Console reads (key: tenant|route|model|window_start).

Observability: emit traffic, error, lag, and reconciliation metrics. Add sanity checks for negative deltas, anomalous p95 regressions, and high variance in sample weights.
data_model:
Fields emitted per window (strings):
- window_start_ts
- window_duration_minutes
- tenant_id
- route_id
- model_id
- request_count
- total_tokens_in
- total_tokens_out
- compute_ms_total
- avg_latency_ms
- p50_latency_ms
- p95_latency_ms
- sample_weight_sum
- inferred_cost_usd_cents
- correction_flag

Schema must remain flat to simplify rollup merges. All numeric fields are stored as integers (milliseconds, token counts, micro-cents).
rollout_plan:
Phase 1 (canary): 1% of routes -> stream path only; validate against existing daily batch reports for 7 days.
Phase 2 (expand): 10% of tenants + critical customers (billing customers) for 14 days; enable low-latency index reads for Console.
Phase 3 (full): enable federated rollups for all tenants and switch Console to read new index.
Rollback: keep previous batch artifacts untouched and allow Console to read either index via a feature flag. Monitor discrepancy metric and abort if >0.5% drift in total cost attribution.
migration_strategy: Run side-by-side: streaming rollups feed into a staging index while the existing batch pipeline remains source-of-truth. During canary, run nightly reconciliation job that compares totals by tenant/route/model and reports diffs. Once drift is within threshold for two weeks, switch read path. Provide a one-time backfill tool for historical windows with delta detection to avoid double-counting.
testing_plan: Unit tests for aggregation logic (sample-weight reconciling), integration tests that run synthetic traces through the stream -> rollup -> index path, performance tests for 5m and hourly windows at expected QPS with headroom, and chaos tests for out-of-order events and duplicate deliveries. Add SQL-based golden-test comparisons against the legacy batch pipeline using a representative 7-day trace sample.
observability_requirements: Produce metrics: rollup_latency_seconds, rollup_failure_count, lag_seconds, stale_window_count, reconciliation_drift_percent. Traces: end-to-end trace propagation from ingestion to index write. Alerts: P0 alert if lag_seconds > 600 for >5m across >20% shards, P1 alert for reconciliation_drift_percent > 1% for >30m.
security_and_privacy_considerations: Ensure tenant IDs are hashed when writing to shared debug topics. No customer PII in rollup artifacts. Rollups contain only aggregated counters. Add RBAC gating for manual backfill and retention exports. Coordinate with Privacy and Security for export retention policy (90 days in hot index, 2 years in cold Parquet).
notes: We will evaluate using existing change-log topic (kafka-infer-telemetry) vs dedicated rollup topic to minimize cross-impact. Early experiments suggest sample-weight reconciliation reduces attribution error vs naive scaling by sampling ratio. Consider adding kernel-cost coefficients provided by runtime team to improve inferred_cost_usd_cents accuracy.
